[wimpLink artistId="10586"]Asian Dub Foundation[/wimpLink] formed in 1993 as an outgrowth of the documentary Identical Beat, a film shot at London's Farringdon Community Music House, the site of a series of summer workshops designed to teach Asian children the essentials of music technology. In charge of the workshops were tutor Aniruddha Das and youth worker John Pandit, also a noted DJ; with one of their students, a 15-year-old Bengali rapper named Deedar Zaman, they soon formed a sound system that they called the Asian Dub Foundation. After each adopted an alias -- bassist/tabla player Das became Dr. Das, Pandit became Pandit G, and Zaman became Master D -- they gradually evolved into a working band with the 1994 addition of former [wimpLink artistId="3736674"]Higher Intelligence Agency[/wimpLink] guitarist Steve Chandra Savale, an innovative performer known for tuning his strings to one note like a sitar, turning up the distortion unit, and playing his instrument with a knife, earning him the nickname "Chandrasonic." Emerging in the midst of considerable anti-Asian violence throughout Britain, [wimpLink artistId="10586"]the Foundation[/wimpLink]'s early demos landed them a contract with Nation Records, and they recorded their debut EP, Conscious, in 1994.
Channeling influences ranging from punk to ambient music to Bengali folk songs, [wimpLink artistId="10586"]Asian Dub Foundation[/wimpLink] quickly gained a strong fan base not only among clubgoers but also among the anti-fascist movement, who applauded the group's vocal stand against racism. After earning a reputation as standout live performers, [wimpLink artistId="10586"]the Foundation[/wimpLink] -- who now included dancer Bubble-E and second DJ Sun-J -- won widespread acclaim for the 1995 single "Rebel Warrior." Their first full-length effort, [wimpLink albumId="102761246"]Facts and Fictions[/wimpLink], followed later that same year, and in 1998 [wimpLink artistId="10586"]Asian Dub Foundation[/wimpLink] returned with [wimpLink albumId="82530480"]Rafi's Revenge[/wimpLink]. [wimpLink albumId="82528876"]Community Music[/wimpLink] appeared in mid-2000, followed later that year by another full-length, R.A.F.I. Subsequent [wimpLink artistId="10586"]Asian Dub Foundation[/wimpLink] albums have included Enemy of the Enemy (2003) and Tank (2005). ~ Jason Ankeny
